title: Two Towns Want a New Bridge for Bikes and Walkers
summary:
The Market Street Bridge crosses the Ohio River. It connects Steubenville, Ohio, with Weirton, West Virginia. But the old steel bridge closed in late 2023. It is too rusty to fix.

The bridge was the only safe way for people walking or biking to cross the river. After it closed, some downtown shops got fewer visitors.

People want a new bridge for another reason, too. The river is a big gap in the Great American Rail-Trail. This trail turns old railroad routes into paths for bikes and walkers. It would stretch about 3,700 miles across the country. More than half of it is already built.

Leaders from both political parties support the new bridge. Steubenville's mayor is a Republican. Weirton's mayor is a Democrat. Both say it would help their towns.

Congress has given $87 million so far. But the bridge will cost more. Leaders are asking for more money.
why_it_matters: A safe bridge helps families walk, bike and visit shops in their towns.
